title: opum-lore pane: generation-token the refresh guards at session.end, and correct the tick-skip wording (LCLI-707 round-1 minors)
description:
Filed by lore-cli's session from LCLI-707's round-1 review (two MINOR findings), citing LCLI-707 and DEC-172 (4bi).

(a) CROSS-SESSION GUARD LEAK. `session.end` sets `refreshInFlight = false` while a refresh can still be running, and that running refresh's `finally` clears the flag unconditionally — so a slow refresh spanning a `/clear` can clear the SUBSEQUENT session's guard, allowing two refreshes across the boundary (the stacking the guard exists to prevent). Close it with a per-session generation token, so a stale run cannot touch a newer session's guards.

(b) WORDING. "only clock ticks are skipped in flight" (in docs/reference/lore-pane-mod.md, in CHANGELOG.md's LCLI-705 entry, and in the code comment on the refresh guard) conflates the two guards: the only skip is tick-vs-tick (`tickInFlight`); a tick colliding with an in-flight REFRESH is COALESCED, not skipped. Correct the wording in all three places.

Scope: the refresh/clock guards in hooks/register.tsx and the three wording sites. Not a redesign of the coalescing behaviour LCLI-707 shipped.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The refresh guards are per-session: a refresh still running when session.end fires cannot clear a later session's guard (a per-session generation token, or an equivalent that makes a stale run's cleanup inert).
Proved both ways: a slow refresh spanning session.end plus a new request goes RED without the token and GREEN with it, and both runs are recorded on the task.

The "only clock ticks are skipped in flight" wording is corrected in docs/reference/lore-pane-mod.md, in CHANGELOG.md, and in the code comment on the refresh guard: the only skip is tick-vs-tick, and a tick colliding with an in-flight refresh is coalesced.
